"""Build this week's research corpus into local Qdrant (collection: default).

Schema mirrors existing points: payload = {"document": str, "metadata": {...}}
Vector: 384-dim MiniLM (fastembed) under name "fast-all-minilm-l6-v2".

Duplicate check: scroll all existing points, skip if arxiv_id is present in
any payload; additionally verify no stored document contains the title.
"""
import json
import urllib.request
import uuid

import fastembed

QDRANT = "http://localhost:6333"
COLL = "default"
VECTOR_NAME = "fast-all-minilm-l6-v2"
DATE = "2026-08-17"
TOPICS = {
    "quantum": "Quantum computing: algorithms, error correction, hardware, quantum ML",
    "materials": "Materials science: DFT, ML interatomic potentials, crystal structure generation",
    "mlsystems": "ML systems: inference efficiency, quantization, MoE architectures, long context",
    "agents": "Agents: tool use, retrieval, evaluation, multi-agent systems",
}

# (topic, arxiv_id, title, one-sentence finding in our own words)
PAPERS = [
    ("quantum", "2608.13975", "Neural decoders for subsystem many-hypercube codes",
     "Recurrent neural decoders for subsystem many-hypercube codes beat fully-connected nets, work on longer syndrome sequences than they were trained on, and can even exploit gauge-measurement information when the syndrome schedule is arranged carefully"),
    ("quantum", "2608.14002", "Circuit Depth Compression via Spectral Gap Amplification in Quantum Phase Estimation",
     "Pre-filtering the operator with a sigmoid spectral step amplifies the effective spectral gap, compressing QPE circuit depth up to 27x and CX count up to 21x, improving LiH output fidelity from 0.66 to 0.98 at a 1% hardware error rate"),
    ("quantum", "2608.14214", "Exchange-only qubit stabilized by a single-spin qubit",
     "Pairing a singlet-only exchange-only qubit with an auxiliary spin converts charge and nuclear noise into erasures and supports fault-tolerant pi-rotations, a new fault-tolerance route for semiconductor spin qubits"),
    ("quantum", "2608.14083", "Information-Calibrated Quantum Diffusion: Aligning Forward Noise with Reverse Recoverability",
     "Calibrating quantum diffusion schedules by information decrement instead of channel strength yields a minimax-coherent forward path and, on a 4-qubit TFIM, lower Wasserstein distance than QuDDPM with fewer parameters"),
    ("materials", "2608.14502", "Universal Thermodynamic Interatomic Potentials for Crystalline Materials",
     "TIP extends a neural interatomic potential into a thermodynamically consistent Gibbs free energy model via automatic differentiation, letting a single evaluation return a crystal's equation of state, phase transitions, and alloy solubility windows for high-throughput finite-temperature screening"),
    ("materials", "2608.14153", "Electrostatic Phenomenology Benchmarks for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials in Electrochemistry: Beyond the Energy-Force Metric",
     "EPhEct is a benchmark of qualitative electrostatic tests - image charge, optical phonon splitting, interfacial dipoles, Fermi-level pinning - that catch MLIP errors aggregate force metrics miss"),
    ("materials", "2608.14147", "Accurate and efficient calculation of atomic forces in solids with non-self-consistent hybrid functionals",
     "Computing hybrid-exchange force corrections once, non-self-consistently via DFPT, cuts the cost of hybrid functional forces in solids while keeping vibrational frequencies within ~0.5%"),
    ("materials", "2608.13038", "Machine-learned interatomic potential for sputtering of tungsten-boron surfaces",
     "A DFT-trained ML potential for W-B systems enables large-scale sputtering MD, showing boron deposition forms a dense boron layer and that surface orientation and composition measurably change the sputter yield"),
    ("materials", "2608.12787", "Finite-Temperature Thermodynamics of Cu(100) Oxidation: Missing-Row Reconstruction, Defect States, and Order-Disorder Transition from Nested Sampling",
     "GPU-accelerated nested sampling with ML interatomic potentials captures the full finite-temperature evolution of early Cu(100) oxidation, including the (2sqrt2 x sqrt2)R45 missing-row reconstruction and its order-disorder transition"),
    ("mlsystems", "2608.14385", "DeaMoE: Efficient MoE Structure for Fast Small-Batch Decoding",
     "Grouping MoE experts into parameter-sharing departments with two-stage routing cuts loaded expert weights by up to 50.9% and gives up to 2x peak TPOT speedups on DeepSeek-V3 during small-batch decoding"),
    ("mlsystems", "2608.14205", "FreeBalance: Pre-Routing Online MoE Load Balancing via Residual Workload Prediction",
     "Predicting upcoming router workload from cross-layer residual-stream similarity lets FreeBalance move experts before routing, hiding balancing latency and cutting max-to-mean load ratio by 32.8% and prefill latency by 13.1%"),
    ("mlsystems", "2608.14191", "KV Cache Compression Through the Lens of Transform Coding",
     "AATC applies transform coding and rate-distortion water-filling with an attention-aware distortion objective, reaching near-lossless quality at ~5.8x KV cache compression on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen-2.5-7B across long-context benchmarks"),
    ("mlsystems", "2608.13966", "QUASAR: Lowering the Loss Floor of Quantization-Aware Training with Loss-Aware Reconstruction",
     "Continuous lightweight loss-aware reconstruction inside the QAT loop lowers the quantized-model loss floor, beating competitive QAT at 2-4 bits and adding 3.5-4.3 accuracy points at 2 bits while supporting standard INT or NVFP4 deployment"),
    ("agents", "2608.14375", "Wrong but Useful: Trajectory Value Beyond Answer Correctness in Multi-Agent Messages",
     "Controlled replay shows that wrong-but-useful messages measurably improve downstream reasoning in multi-agent systems, so keeping them can beat filtering on answer correctness alone"),
    ("agents", "2608.14107", "Retrieval Grounding Latent Reasoning for Dense Retrieval",
     "RGLT grounds silent-token latent reasoning trajectories in per-stage credit for actual retrieval gains, avoiding the shortcut reasoning that purely output-supervised reasoning embeddings learn"),
]

assert len(PAPERS) == 15

# ---- existing data scan (duplicate check) ----
req = urllib.request.Request(f"{QDRANT}/{COLL}/points/scroll",
                             data=json.dumps({"limit": 100, "with_payload": True}).encode())
existing = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))["result"]["points"]
stored_docs = [p["payload"].get("document", "") for p in existing]
stored_arxiv = set()
for p in existing:
    aid = (p["payload"].get("metadata") or {}).get("arxiv_id")
    if aid:
        stored_arxiv.add(aid)
    doc = p["payload"].get("document", "") or ""
    for tok in doc.split():
        if tok.startswith("arXiv:") and len(tok) > 6:
            stored_arxiv.add(tok[6:])
print(f"existing points: {len(existing)}, arxiv ids seen: {len(stored_arxiv)}")

# ---- embeds ----
model = fastembed.TextEmbedding()  # all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim
print("model ready")

# ---- store ----
to_store, skipped = [], []
for topic, arxiv_id, title, finding in PAPERS:
    if arxiv_id in stored_arxiv:
        skipped.append((title, arxiv_id, "arxiv_id already stored"))
        continue
    if any(title.lower() in d.lower() for d in stored_docs):
        skipped.append((title, arxiv_id, "title already stored"))
        continue
    info = f"{title}. {finding}. arXiv:{arxiv_id}"
    to_store.append({
        "id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
        "vector_name": VECTOR_NAME,
        "payload": {
            "document": info,
            "metadata": {
                "topic": TOPICS[topic],
                "arxiv_id": arxiv_id,
                "date": DATE,
                "source": "arxiv-weekly",
            },
        },
    })

skipped_lines = [f"SKIP {s[0]} - {s[2]}" for s in skipped]
print("\n".join(skipped_lines) if skipped else "no duplicates skipped")

if to_store:
    vectors = list(model.embed([t["payload"]["document"] for t in to_store]))
    body = json.dumps({
        "points": [
            {"id": t["id"], "vector": v, "payload": t["payload"]}
            for t, v in zip(to_store, vectors)
        ],
        "wait": True,
    }).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"{QDRANT}/collections/{COLL}/points", data=body,
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    resp = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))
    statuses = resp.get("result", {}).get("statuses", [])
    print("stored:", len(to_store), "statuses:", statuses)
    with open("stored_ids.txt", "w") as f:
        for t in to_store:
            f.write(f"{t['payload']['metadata']['topic']}\t{t['payload']['metadata']['arxiv_id']}\t{t['payload']['document'].split('.')[0]}\n")

# ---- verify ----
check = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(
    f"{QDRANT}/collections/{COLL}/points/count" and
    urllib.request.Request(
        f"{QDRANT}/collections/{COLL}/points/scroll",
        data=json.dumps({"filter": {"must": [{"key": "metadata.source", "match": {"value": "arxiv-weekly"}}]}}).encode(),
    )))
arxiv_weekly = [p["payload"]["document"].split(". arXiv:")[1] for p in check["result"]["points"]]
print("arxiv-weekly points now in corpus:", len(arxiv_weekly))
print("this run stored still verifiable:", sum(1 for t in to_store if t["id"] in arxiv_weekly), "/", len(to_store))

While a wide range of decoding algorithms have been proposed and demonstrated, achieving reliable, scalable, and real-time decoding remains a significant challenge. Machine-learning (ML) approaches are particularly well suited to this setting, as quantum error decoding is fundamentally a problem of processing large volumes of classical data with complex spatiotemporal correlations.
